inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: Martin is pointing to increased tenancies, but that’s exactly the kind of reassuring number that can be used to steer attention away from what’s getting worse: eviction notices and homelessness are rising, and emergency accommodation numbers nationally have climbed again. The six-year lease rules introduced by the Government on March 1 may be part of the machinery behind this, not proof that the crisis is being solved. They want people to see more tenancies and stop asking who is being pushed out—and why.
